gaps.where: AI teammate (web): the tabs Teammate · Instructions · Funnels · Review · Activity · Approvals. The Teammate tab's left-hand list sits in three groups: Basics (Identity, Channels, Hours), What it does (Respond, Answer, Qualify, Book, Follow up, Add-ons) and Rules and safety (Hand-off, Autonomy, Limits). Run quick setup again sits under the list.
gaps.gap: The AI teammate screen has six tabs: Teammate, Instructions, Funnels, Review, Activity and Approvals. Its sections sit in three groups (Basics; What it does, which includes Add-ons; Rules and safety), with Run quick setup again under them. The settings map's ai_teammate entry says 'Tabs: Teammate, Activity, Approvals'. TEAMMATE_SECTIONS lists 11 sections in an old flat order, with no groups and no Add-ons section. Nothing in settings-map.ts, places-map.ts, prompt.ts or context.ts mentions funnels, the Instructions or Review tabs, or Run quick setup again. prompt.ts:38 tells the model never to name a place or tab that isn't listed. So for 'where do I build a funnel / teach it a rule / see what it learned?' the Assistant either says it isn't sure or gives the wrong tab list, even though the do_funnel_*, do_teammate_instruction_*, do_teammate_lesson_* and read_ai_teammate_review / read_teammate_instruction_list / read_funnel_* tools exist.

gaps.where: AI teammate → Funnels, a funnel's builder: the Stages, Messages, Wording and Who steps, then Save (or Save and close).
gaps.gap: Changing a funnel through do_funnel_save means sending the revision and the whole FunnelDefinition. That is how the screen's save works too, so re-sending every stage is not a gap by itself. The real part: read_funnel_get answers through runScreenRead, which cuts any answer over 16,000 characters of JSON into a string with cutShort. funnel.get takes only funnelId, so there is no way to ask for less. Its answer holds the whole definition (up to 12 stages, each with a 1,000-character 'knows' and up to 8 messages of 1,000 characters) plus counts, issues and the business's forms and calendars. So for a medium-to-large funnel, the Assistant can't see the whole definition, and can't safely change one message or stage without dropping the rest. Small funnels work.
gaps.fix:
Add a worker tool, change_funnel (confirm, ai_team.manage), in a new section of apps/worker/src/assistant/tools-content.ts:
- It takes funnelId plus one targeted change: rename, a stage's goal or knows, add/change/remove one message by id, add/remove a move, an entry rule, or byHand/aiSuggests.
- It reads funnel.get itself for the current definition and revision, applies the change, and runs funnel.save.
- Its card names the funnel and the stage or message that changes.

Or give funnel.get an optional stageId (FunnelGetInput, packages/core/src/schemas/funnel.ts:212) that returns only that stage's definition, so a stage always reads whole.

gaps.where: Run quick setup again (web: under the teammate's sections; phone: More → Set up your AI teammate). On the last step, Turn on adds the website chat to the business's simple booking page.
gaps.gap: Quick setup on the screen sends pageOrigin, the booking page's branded or public origin. Then a business with no website of its own gets its website chat on its simple page. do_ai_setup_finish (and do_onboarding_setup_finish) expose pageOrigin as an optional model argument, but the model has no source for it: read_ai_setup_get returns no origin, and nothing in the prompt names one. Without it the command skips the chat and only pushes a note, which the confirmed path then throws away (tm-5). The worker already knows how to work out this origin elsewhere. This lowers severity: it hits only businesses with a page and no website, and the chat can be added later.

gaps.where: The Assistant's 'Do this?' card for saving or creating a funnel, for quick setup's finish, and for other screen commands with nested input.
gaps.gap:
Every do_* screen action draws its 'Do this?' card with cardFields/valueOf: one line per input key, labelled from the key.
- An object becomes clipped JSON, and an array of objects becomes 'N items'.
- uuids and revisions show as they are.

So do_funnel_save shows 'Funnel id: <uuid>', 'Revision: 4', 'Definition: {"description":…' clipped at 300 characters, and 'Move from: {…}'. do_funnel_create shows 'Draft: {…}', and do_ai_setup_finish shows 'Answers: {…}' and 'Base revision'. The person can't see which stages or messages change, and the card shows ids, which the house rules forbid.

gaps.where: AI teammate → Approvals: every waiting draft (the page loads up to 100) and the Decided view of drafts decided lately.
gaps.gap: The Approvals tab loads up to 100 waiting drafts and the last 30 decided ones. list_teammate_drafts always asks for status 'pending', at most 20, with no cursor, no nextCursor and no 'more are waiting' note. ai_teammate.draft_list is not a screen read, and no other Assistant tool reads decided drafts (who decided, edits, reason, decidedAt). So 'what did Ava send yesterday that Sam approved?' and 'why was that one rejected?' can't be answered. With more than 20 waiting, the Assistant believes it saw them all. The query already supports status 'decided'/'all' and a cursor.

gaps.where: AI teammate → Test console (Test as a customer; By text, chat, email or phone; At now or a picked time; Start over). Also quick setup's test questions, and the phone's More → Test your AI teammate.
gaps.gap: No Assistant tool can put a test question to the teammate and report its reply and the actions it would take. The test console (web, quick setup's try step, and the phone) runs through the worker's POST /v1/ai-team/test with ai_team.manage. Test runs send nothing to customers, and the Activity screen marks them isTest. The settings map only hands it back to the person ('Try it as a customer: AI teammate, Test console'). Nothing in NEVER_FOR_THE_ASSISTANT or SETTINGS_NEVER says why not. One thing to note: a test does use the business's AI share (the route returns 429 at the limit).
gaps.fix:
Add a worker tool, test_ai_teammate: autonomy auto, permission ai_team.manage, spec in packages/core/src/assistant/tools-extra.ts.
- Inputs: messages (the customer's words, up to TEST_MESSAGES_MAX turns), channel ('sms'|'email'|'chat'; leave out 'phone', which is a live call), optional at (ISO time), optional personId.
- It calls prepareTest/runTest from apps/worker/src/ai-team/console.ts with config null (the saved settings), collects the ConsoleEvent stream, and returns the reply text, the tools it would call with their summaries, and any hand-off.
- Its description says it sends nothing and counts toward the AI limit.

Then change settings-map.ts:894's howTo to 'Try it as a customer: AI teammate, Test console (or ask me to try a question)'.

gaps.where: AI teammate → Qualify: the up and down arrows on each question, which set the order it asks them in.
gaps.gap: Qualify's questions have up and down arrows that set the order. update_ai_teammate_rules can add (always at the end), change or remove questions, but can't move one. gaps.where: AI teammate → Book: 'What <calendar> is for' under each calendar (up to 2,000 characters, and it can be emptied).
gaps.gap: The Book section's 'What <calendar> is for' saves the calendar's description through calendar.save. It allows up to 2,000 characters, and an empty box saves null. manage_calendar's description is text(500): trimmed, at least 1 and at most 500 characters. The worker passes it only through str(). So the Assistant can't write a purpose over 500 characters, and can't clear one. calendar.save is not a screen action either.
gaps.fix: In packages/core/src/assistant/tools.ts:379, make manage_calendar's description `z.string().trim().max(2000).nullable().optional().describe('What the calendar is for, which the AI teammate reads; null clears it')`. In apps/worker/src/assistant/tools-settings-calendar.ts:338-342, pass `description: args['description'] === null ? null : str(args['description'])`, and make `defined()` keep null.

gaps.where: AI teammate → Qualify (its switch) and Limits.
gaps.gap:
Two tool descriptions disagree about who owns Qualify and Limits.
- manage_ai_teammate's description says it changes 'what it may do (respond, answer questions, qualify, book, follow up) and its limits'. It has no qualify or limits inputs.
- update_ai_teammate_rules' description holds the Qualify switch (qualifies) and every limit. Yet it says 'its skills on or off are manage_ai_teammate'.

So the model can pick the wrong tool for 'turn off qualifying' or 'cap replies a day', or tell the person it can't.
gaps.fix: In packages/core/src/assistant/tools.ts:1020, change '(respond, answer questions, qualify, book, follow up) and its limits' to '(respond, answer questions, book, follow up); the Qualify skill, its questions and its limits are update_ai_teammate_rules'.
